text: No, the 2025 loss is not yet confirmed as persistent. The evidence shows a 13.5 ha tree-cover loss in 2025, but this is the latest year in the dataset, so we cannot confirm if the loss remains in later years. The assessment is still pending corroboration—we’d need data from 2026 or beyond to determine if the loss is permanent. The cause (e.g., fire, logging, or natural disturbance) also remains unclear. While the area was mostly native forest in 2020, the change could be temporary (e.g., regrowth after harvesting). Further monitoring is required to confirm persistence.
